title: pertMean computes the weighted PERT mean (min + 4*likely + max) / 6
samplePERT returns exactly range.min when max equals min, with no NaN or divide-by-zero
description: samplePERT has an explicit short-circuit `if (range.max === range.min) return range.min;` before any normalization math that would otherwise divide by (max-min)=0.
expectedResult: Returns exactly 5000 — no NaN, no thrown error, no dependency on the rng function being called.

title: createSeededRandom produces an identical sequence for the same seed
description: The mulberry32 PRNG backing createSeededRandom must be fully deterministic so an auditor can reproduce a previously stored Monte Carlo simulation result exactly.
steps: Call createSeededRandom(42) again (a fresh instance) and draw 5 values
expectedResult: Both 5-value sequences are exactly identical, element for element.

title: buildRiskDistribution prioritizes the flat riskDistribution tier over the nested vendorStats.byRiskTier tier
description: applyFlatDistribution returns true (short-circuiting the fallback chain) on the first non-zero match; when the dashboard's flat riskDistribution and analytics' nested vendorStats.byRiskTier are both present with different values, the flat one must win.
steps: Call buildRiskDistribution(dash, analytics) where dash.riskDistribution = { critical: 2, high: 3, medium: 1, low: 0 } and analytics.data.vendorStats.byRiskTier = { critical: 9, high: 9, medium: 9, low: 9 }
expectedResult: Returned distribution is { critical: 2, high: 3, medium: 1, low: 0 } — the flat tier's values, not the nested tier's.

title: Security Score composite renormalizes weights when a sub-score is unavailable rather than zero-filling it
description: ExecutiveDashboardService builds validScores only from non-null sub-scores (technical 0.35 / process 0.25 / governance 0.20 / people 0.20) and divides by totalWeight of just those present — verifies a missing people score reweights the remaining 3 scores over their own 0.80 total instead of silently averaging in a 0.
steps: Compute the composite with technicalScore=80, processScore=60, governanceScore=100, peopleScore=null
expectedResult: Composite = round((80*0.35 + 60*0.25 + 100*0.20) / 0.80) = round(78.75) = 79 — not round((80*0.35 + 60*0.25 + 100*0.20 + 0*0.20)) = 63, which would incorrectly treat the missing score as a 0.
